title: Minnesota Company Recalls Fresh Cut Cantaloupe Over Listeria Concerns - NewsBreak
text:
10 hours ago MINNEAPOLIS, Minn. – Wholesale Produce Supply, based in Minneapolis, has issued a recall of fresh cut and processed cantaloupe due to concerns the fruit may be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes. The announcement was posted September 29, 2025, by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as a public service.
Photo by Martin Moore on Unsplash “Wholesale Produce Supply of Minneapolis, Minnesota is recalling fresh cut/processed cantaloupe, because it has the potential to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes, an organism which can cause serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, frail or elderly people, and others with weakened immune systems,” the company said in its announcement.
The recalled cantaloupe was distributed to Nebraska, North Dakota, and Wisconsin, and may have reached additional states. It was sold under the “Harvest Cuts” and “Fresh and Finest” brands at traditional grocery stores. The products came in plastic clamshell containers and included both cantaloupe-only packages and mixed fruit containers.
No illnesses linked to the cantaloupe have been reported at this time. According to the company, “The recall was the result of a routine sampling program by the company which revealed that the finished products potentially contained bacteria. Wholesale Produce Supply has suspended production and distribution of the affected lots as the company continues their investigation as to what caused the problem.”
Consumers are urged to return affected “Harvest Cuts” or “Fresh and Finest” products to the place of purchase for a full refund. Anyone with questions can contact Steve Foster, Vice President of Food Safety and Quality Assurance, at (612) 378-2025 or by email at sfoster@wpsfresh.com .
